extracted.intended_audience: breeders, plant variety registrants, IP practitioners, and state agency staff involved in plant variety protection in Vietnam
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation criteria for obtaining, maintaining, challenging, and exercising rights in plant variety protection in Vietnam, including substantive DUS (distinctness, uniformity, stability) requirements, formal application requirements, procedural deadlines, and rights/limitations. Useful for applicants, attorneys, testers, and administrative officials handling plant variety protection applications and certificates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (newness) of plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: A plant variety is deemed new if reproductive materials or harvested materials of such variety have not yet been sold or otherwise distributed for the purpose of exploitation in the Vietnamese territory by the registration right holder or his/her licensee one year before the filing date; or for exploitation outside Vietnam six years before the filing date for timber trees and vines, and four years for other plant varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty is assessed by prior sale/distribution by the registration right holder or licensee; different time-limits apply for domestic (1 year) and foreign exploitation (6 years for timber/vines, 4 years for others).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctness of plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: A variety is distinct if it is clearly distinguishable from any other variety whose existence is a matter of common knowledge at the time of filing or priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common knowledge includes: (a) reproductive/harvested materials widely used in any country's market at filing time; (b) varieties protected/registered in any country; (c) varieties subject to pending or registered protection applications in any country (not rejected); (d) varieties with published detailed descriptions. Distinctness is judged against these known varieties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: A plant variety is deemed uniform if, subject to the variation expected from its particular method of propagation, it is sufficiently uniform in its relevant characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors consider expected propagation-related variation; uniformity must be 'sufficient' in relevant characteristics for the species and propagation method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability of plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: A plant variety is deemed stable if its relevant originally described characteristics remain unchanged after repeated propagation or, for a particular cycle, at the end of each cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability is demonstrated by repeated propagation cycles or end-of-cycle observations showing unchanged characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper denomination of plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant must designate a denomination that is the same as the denomination registered in any country upon filing and is distinguishable from denominations of other varieties of common knowledge in the same or similar species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denominations are improper if: (a) numerals only (unless numerals relevant to characteristics/breeding); (b) violate social ethics; (c) likely to mislead as to features/characteristics; (d) likely to mislead as to breeder identification; (e) identical or confusingly similar to marks/trade names/geographical indications protected before publication date; (f) identical/similar to denominations of harvested materials of such varieties; (g) affect prior rights of others. Denominations used in marketing must follow registered denomination even after protection expiry. When combined with trademarks/trade names, denominations must still be distinguishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to be a registrant (who may register)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants include: (a) breeders who personally selected and bred or discovered and developed the varieties with own efforts and expenses; (b) organizations/individuals that funded breeders under job assignment or hiring unless otherwise agreed; (c) assignees or heirs of the registration right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For varieties developed with state budget or under state-managed projects, rights belong to the State; the Government will specify registration for such cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of filing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Vietnamese organizations/individuals and foreign entities with permanent residence addresses or production/trading establishments in Vietnam may file directly or through lawful representatives; foreign entities without such presence must file through lawful representatives in Vietnam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative power of attorney requirements apply when filing through representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-to-file principle
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple parties independently file protection applications on different days for the same variety, the protection certificate is granted only to the earliest valid registrant; when filed the same day, certificate is granted to the registrant whose name is used for the sole application agreed upon by all registrants, or failing agreement, to the party determined to be the first breeder who selected/bred or discovered/developed the variety.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing of filings determines priority except where same-day filings require agreement or determination of first breeder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority claiming and proof
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant may claim priority if filing within 12 months from the first filing in a country that has an agreement with Vietnam; the claim must be expressed in the application. Within 3 months after filing the Vietnam application, the registrant must produce certified copies of the first application and samples or other evidence proving both applications concern the same variety and pay the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If needed, the registrant may supply necessary documents/materials for examination within 2 years after expiration of the priority duration, or within an appropriate duration after the first application is rejected or withdrawn. When eligible, the priority date is the first filing date. Filing or publication within the 12-month period does not count as a ground for rejecting the priority-eligible application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of a protection certificate and national register entry
rubrics_metrics.description: A protection certificate must state the variety denomination and species, the name of the owner (protection certificate holder), the breeder's name, and the protection term. The state agency shall record grants and contents in the national register and archive the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate content requirements are mandatory for the grant and registration process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity period of protection certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection certificates are valid throughout Vietnamese territory from grant date to the end of: 25 years for timber trees and vines; 20 years for other plant varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates may be terminated or invalidated per law; these durations are statutory maximum terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for termination of certificate validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Validity may be terminated if: (a) the protected variety no longer satisfies uniformity and stability as at grant time; (b) holder fails to pay validity maintenance fee; (c) holder fails to supply necessary documents and reproductive materials for maintaining/preserving the variety; (d) holder fails to change the denomination at the agency's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency issues termination decisions in cases (a),(c),(d). For nonpayment (b), termination is from first day of next valid year for which maintenance fee is unpaid. Any party may request termination under (a). Agency must publish termination reasons and notify holder; holder has 30 days to request remedies and pay restoration fee, and 90 days to remedy (in cases b,c,d). Restoration requires proof of satisfaction of uniformity/stability and certification by the state agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for invalidation of certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate shall be invalidated if: (a) the application was filed in the name of a person without the registration right (unless right assigned to the holder); (b) the protected variety failed to satisfy novelty or distinctness at grant time; (c) variety failed to satisfy uniformity or stability where certificate was granted based on registrant-conducted technical tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any organization or individual may request invalidation during the valid term. If invalidated, all transactions arising on the basis of the invalid certificate are null and void and handled per Civil Code. Agency considers requests and opinions before invalidation/refusal to invalidate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification and re-grant of certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Holders may request correction/modification of errors related to names and addresses (fees apply) unless error was made by the agency, in which case agency must correct without charging fees. Holders may request re-grant where certificates are lost/damaged subject to fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures require payment of prescribed fees unless error originates from agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of decisions related to certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions on grant, re-grant, termination of validity, invalidation or modification must be published by the state management agency in a specialized magazine on plant varieties within 60 days after issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is an administrative requirement for transparency and public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of a protection registration application
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must include: (a) a declaration form made according to set form; (b) photos and technical declarations per set form; (c) power of attorney if filed through a representative; (d) documents evidencing registration right if registrant is transferee; (e) documents evidencing priority right where claimed; (f) vouchers of payment of fees and charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications and transactional documents must be in Vietnamese, except certain documents (power of attorney, documents evidencing registration right, priority right, other supporting documents) may be in another language but must be translated into Vietnamese at the agency's request. Documents evidencing priority include certified copies of first applications and transfer/inheritance papers. Each application must be for protection of one plant variety only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt criteria and filing date
rubrics_metrics.description: An application is received by the agency only when enclosed with all documents specified. The filing date is the date the application is received by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete applications are not accorded a filing date; ensure all prescribed documents accompany submission to obtain filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal examination and invalidity grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency must conduct formal examination within 15 days after receipt to determine validity. An application is invalid if: (a) it fails to satisfy formal requirements; (b) the plant variety does not belong to a species on the list of protected plant species; (c) it is filed by a person without registration right, including where co-owners disagree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency procedures include notifying refusal for case (b) or (c) with reasons; notifying the registrant of errors for correction for case (a) and setting a 30-day correction limit; notifying refusal if registrant fails to correct or does not reasonably appeal; notifying acceptance and requesting samples for technical tests where valid or errors properly corrected/justifiably opposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of accepted applications
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is accepted as valid, the agency shall publish it in a specialized magazine on plant varieties within 90 days from acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published content must include serial number and filing date, representative agent (if any), registrant, owner, denomination, species name, and date accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination coverage (DUS and denomination)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination covers: (a) examination of novelty and proper denominations; (b) examination of results of technical tests of plant varieties. Technical tests are experiments to determine distinctness, uniformity and stability (DUS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical tests are to be conducted by competent state agencies or capable organizations/individuals per Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development regulations; the state agency may use previously obtained technical test results. Time limit for examination of technical test results is 90 days from receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights to modify or supplement applications before decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a decision (grant or refusal), the registrant may: (a) modify or supplement the application without changing its nature; (b) request recording of changes in name or address; (c) request recording of change of registrant due to assignment, inheritance or bequest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for these procedures require payment of fees and charges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of protection registration application
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the agency decides or refuses, a registrant may withdraw the application by written request. From withdrawal, all subsequent procedures stop; fees/charges already paid for procedures not yet carried out shall be refunded at the registrant's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal halts processing and may entitle to refund for unperformed procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party opinions on grant
rubrics_metrics.description: From publication of an application until before a decision on grant, any third party may submit written opinions challenging the grant, accompanied by documents and evidence to support them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions must be in writing and supported by evidence; they are considered during examination and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for refusal to grant certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall be rejected if the variety fails to satisfy formal and substantive conditions. Agency procedures: (1) notify intended refusal with reasons and set time for registrant to correct or oppose; (2) notify refusal if registrant fails to correct or oppose; (3) follow procedures for grant if registrant corrects errors or makes justifiable opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must clearly state reasons for intended refusal and provide opportunity to correct within the set time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Granting of plant variety protection certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is not rejected and the registrant pays the fee, the agency shall decide to grant a protection certificate and record it in the national register of protected plant varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment of prescribed fees is a condition precedent to grant and registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint and appeal rights regarding grants/refusals
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants and any third party may complain about decisions or refusals to grant protection certificates. Settlement of complaints follows the law on complaints and denunciations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative or judicial recourse available per general complaint/litigation laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and scope of breeders' and certificate holders' rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Breeder rights: to have breeder name recorded in certificate, register, and published documents; to receive remunerations per law or agreement. Protection certificate holder rights: to exercise or authorize acts concerning reproductive materials (produce/propagate, process for propagation, offer for sale, sell/market, export, import, stock) and to prevent others from using the variety per infringement provisions; rights transferable by inheritance or transfer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights extend to varieties originating from the protected variety (subject to definition), varieties not definitely distinct, and varieties requiring repeated use of the protected variety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts constituting infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringements include: (1) exploiting/using rights without permission; (2) using a denomination identical or similar to a protected denomination for same or closely linked species; (3) using a protected variety without paying required remuneration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated acts serve as baselines for enforcement and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rights between publication and grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional rights arise from date of publication of the protection registration application until grant; they do not exist if certificate is not granted. Registrants aware of commercial use by others may notify users of filing and publication dates; upon grant, the certificate holder may request compensation equivalent to licensing price for corresponding scope/duration for prior commercial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification in writing specifying filing and publication dates precedes compensation claims. Compensation claims apply after grant if prior use continued after notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations/exceptions to protection holders' rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts not regarded as infringements include: (a) use for personal/non-commercial purposes; (b) use for crossbreeding for scientific research; (c) use to create new distinct varieties; (d) using harvested materials by individual production households for self-propagation and cultivation on their own land for next season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rights do not apply to acts related to materials of protected varieties once sold or brought to market by holders or licensees, except for further propagation and export to countries where the genus/species is not protected (unless exported for consumption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of protection certificate holders and breeders
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection certificate holders must: (a) pay remunerations to breeders as agreed or per law; (b) pay maintenance fees for validity; (c) preserve protected varieties, supply reproductive materials to the state agency, and maintain stability per regulations. Breeders must assist holders in maintaining reproductive materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet obligations (e.g., payment, supply of materials) is grounds for termination of validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and contractual requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensing means permission by the certificate holder for another to conduct one or several acts of the holder's rights. Licensing of co-owned rights requires consent of all co-owners. Licensing must be in written contract which must not contain terms unreasonably restricting licensee's rights, especially restrictions not deriving from protecting licensor's rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts must be written; unreasonable restrictive terms are prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights and remedies of licensee and licensor in license contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensor may permit or deny sublicensing. Licensee rights include: (a) sublicensing if permitted; (b) requesting licensor to take measures against third-party infringements causing damage to licensee; (c) taking necessary measures to prevent infringement if licensor fails to act within 3 months of request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee can act to protect its interests if licensor does not timely pursue infringements after being requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of rights to plant varieties
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment transfers all rights from certificate holder to assignee; assignee becomes certificate holder from the date of registration of assignment contract with the state agency. Joint ownership assignments require consent of all co-owners. Assignment must be in written contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration of the assignment with the state agency is required for effectivity of transfer of certificate holder status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory licensing bases and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent state agency may license use to others without permission of the holder in cases: (a) use for public interest/non-commercial purposes serving national defense, security, food security/nutrition or other urgent social needs; (b) applicants with demand/capacity fail to reach agreement with holder despite best efforts within reasonable time; (c) holder engages in anti-competitive practices per competition law. Conditions for compulsory license: non-exclusive; scope/duration limited to achieve objectives (largely domestic market); licensee cannot assign or sub-license (except with business transfer); licensee must pay adequate compensation taking into account economic value and government compensation rate brackets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government to specify cases and compensation rate brackets. Holder may request termination of licensed use when bases cease and are unlikely to recur, provided termination is not prejudicial to licensee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence and procedures for compulsory licensing decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Agriculture and Rural Development Ministry issues decisions on licensing in fields under its management; other ministries issue decisions in their fields after consulting the Agriculture Ministry. Licensing decisions must set use scope and conditions per statutory requirements. Competent agency must promptly notify holders of exclusive rights; decisions or refusals may be complained about or litigated; Government specifies procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative process and consultation requirements apply; holders are entitled to notification and recourse.
